newsitem.title: CHINA: Chiang Kai-shek's fine taste angers China city.
newsitem.headline: Chiang Kai-shek's fine taste angers China city.

text.p: The taste of the late Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek who would settle for nothing less than the best has triggered outcries in China's former wartime capital, Chongqing, the Beijing Youth Daily said on Monday.
An advertising gimmick by "President" bottled mineral water company to cash in on Chiang's exquisite taste has backfired, the newspaper said.

Many consumers protested against a claim that "President" mineral water came from the same well Chiang reputedly drank from exclusively during his stay in Chongqing in the southwestern province of Sichuan, the newspaper said.

"Chiang Kai-shek's hands are stained with the blood of Communist Party members and the masses. How can any company use him to promote their products," the newspaper quoted one indignant communist army veteran as saying.

But a company official, contacted by telephone, said "President" mineral water was enjoying booming sales. A picture of Chiang's former residence in Chongqing and the words "the style of kings" appear on the bottle's label.
Chiang fled to Taiwan in 1949 after his troops lost the civil war to Mao Zedong's Red Army.
